stem: The 'critical period' is a vital stage in pediatric ophthalmology. During which years of a child's life does the visual system develop and remain most receptive to treatment?
explanation: This period is identified as the time when the visual system is still developing and can be significantly improved through effective clinical intervention.
rationale: Consider the timeframe mentioned as the window of opportunity for changing the visual cortex.

optionExplanations.A: This period is identified as the time when the visual system is still developing and can be significantly improved through effective clinical intervention.
optionExplanations.B: While early infancy is important, the visual system continues to mature and remains plastic for several years beyond the first year.
optionExplanations.C: The critical period for visual development typically concludes around age 8, well before the onset of puberty.
optionExplanations.D: Visual development begins at birth; waiting until age 4 would miss the early years of the critical development window.

source.hint: Consider the timeframe mentioned as the window of opportunity for changing the visual cortex.
